nodes.question: What is the purpose of the reforestation project in the northern part of the Cakalburnu Lagoon?
nodes.answer: The reforestation project aims to establish the Izmir-Inciralt Recreation Area, which covers an area of 200 hectares.
nodes.paragraph: In 2019, the amount of green space per person in Izmir city is 8.6 m2 (Ersoy-Tonyalo lu & Nurlu, 2023). The Cakalburnu Lagoon has experienced a 5.6% loss in Water Air Soil Pollut (2025) 236:208 208 Vol. : (123456789) land use area over a 22-year period between 1996 and 2018 (Kara, 2019). Cakalburnu Lagoon is the most important element of the wetland and hosts 121 bird species (Kaya, 2017). Lagoon systems, in addition to being natural bio- logical resources, serve as natural laboratories for scientific research and play a significant role in the preservation and sustainability of biodiversity in sensitive and fragile ecosystems (Yucel-Gier et al., 2018). The quantity and quality of water in a lagoon are influenced by factors such as evaporation within the lagoon, precipitation, groundwater inflow, sur - face runoff, and the exchange of seawater (Somay, 2016; Somay-Altas, 2021). The Cakalburnu Lagoon is an irreplaceable coastal urban wetland located to the south of Izmir Bay, encompasses an area of approximately 64 hectares and exhibits a shallow depth ranging from 0.5 to 1 m. A reforestation pro- ject in the northern part of the Cakalburnu Lagoon, situated within the study area, has led to the establish- ment of the Izmir-Inciralt Recreation Area cover - ing an area of 200 hectares (Somay-Altas, 2022).

nodes.question: Why is Ghana considered an important case study for understanding REDD+ programs?
nodes.answer: Ghana is significant due to its abundant forest resources, high deforestation rate, and the critical role of cocoa production in its economy, which directly impacts forest landscape management and conservation efforts.
nodes.paragraph: 2015 ; Ameyaw et al. 2016 ). Moreover, the implementation of local REDD +pilot initiatives has often marginalized local community interests, leading to con icts and power struggles between government bodies, corpora- tions, and local communities (Appiah et al. 2015 ; Saeed et al. 2018 ; Soliev et al. 2021 ). These challenging system context conditions may impose considerable limitations on the effectiveness of collaborative natural resource manage-ment and conservation initiatives (Akamani et al. 2015 ). Amid the tumultuous context of Ghana S weak forest gov- ernance system, the establishment and implementation ofREDD+CGR must contend with persistent challenges in adapting to dynamic processes to achieve sustainable social and ecological outcomes (Akamani et al. 2015 ). In this article, the IFCG is used to analyze the effects of the particular dynamics of the system context of forest governance in Ghana S HFZ on the speci C drivers for establishing REDD +CGR. The speci C research questions addressed are: (1) How applicable is the IFCG framework in the context of REDD +programs in developing countries? (2) What conditions are essential to sustain a collaborative REDD+governance approach that effectively bene its both the environment and local communities in developingcountries?
